evals.prompt: I want to add multi-language support to my Flutter app. Which localization package should I use and why?
evals.expected_output: Default recommendation: flutter_localizations + gen-l10n (official Flutter SDK, no extra package, ARB files, compile-time safe). slang as alternative when JSON/YAML format needed or Flutter-independent. NOT easand_localization as default (runtime parsing, less safe). Explains the tradeoffs.

assertions.text: Response recommends flutter_localizations + gen-l10n as the default choice — it is the official Flutter SDK approach requiring no extra package
Response mentions slang as an alternative for type-safe JSON/YAML support, not as the default
Response does NOT recommend easand_localization as the default (it has runtime parsing and is less type-safe)

evals.prompt: We're adding Arabic support to our app. Some of our layouts use EdgeInsets.only(left: 16) for padding. Will this work correctly in RTL mode?
evals.expected_output: No — EdgeInsets.only(left:) is hardcoded to the left, which breaks RTL. Use EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start: 16) instead. 'start' maps to left in LTR and right in RTL automatically. Also use AlignmentDirectional instead of Alignment for alignments.

assertions.text: Response identifies EdgeInsets.only(left:) as problematic for RTL — it always applies to the physical left side
Response recommends EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:) as the correct RTL-aware replacement

evals.prompt: In our app we show messages like '1 item in cart' or '3 items in cart'. How should I handle pluralization in Flutter localization? I don't want to use a ternary operator in my widget code.
evals.expected_output: Uses ICU plural rules in the ARB file (or slang equivalent). The widget just calls l10n.cartItems(count) — the plural form is resolved by the framework. Avoids count == 1 ? 'item' : 'items' in widget code.

assertions.text: Response uses ICU plural rules in the translation file (ARB or equivalent) — not a ternary in widget code
Response shows the widget calling a single localization method with a count parameter — the plural logic is in the translation file
